newsitem.title: CHINA: China's communists to turn 76, blow own horn on HK.
newsitem.headline: China's communists to turn 76, blow own horn on HK.

text.p: China's ruling Communist Party blew its own horn on Monday, the eve of its birthday, crowing that Hong Kong's peaceful return to Chinese sovereignty would not have been possible without the communists.

"The return of Hong Kong to the motherland... has been a dream for more than 100 years but became reality step by step only under the leadership of the Communist Party," the official People's Daily said in a front-page editorial to celebrate the handover.

"With irrefutable facts, history has declared to the world that without the Communist Party of China... the smooth return of Hong Kong could not have been possible," said the mouthpiece of the Communist Party, which celebrates its 76th founding anniversary on Tuesday.

Late paramount leader and communist veteran Deng Xiaoping negotiated the return of capitalist Hong Kong, reaching agreement with London in 1984 to recover the territory, seized after Britain defeated a weak imperial China in the 19th-century "opium wars".

China's communists were upbeat about the territory's future after Beijing recovers sovereignty at midnight on Monday, ignoring concerns among Hong Kong democrats, international human rights groups and some Western governments about the future of the enclave under a communist ruler.

"The return of Hong Kong is the end of 100 years of humiliating history and the beginning of the implementation of a totally new concept," the People's Daily editorial said in a reference to Deng's "one country, two systems" formula.
Under Deng's plan Britain agreed to return Hong Kong to China and Beijing promised that the enclave would keep its capitalist lifestyle for 50 years.

Hong Kong's confidence in that pledge was dented in June, 1989 when Chinese soldiers backed by tanks crushed student-led demonstrations for democracy centred in Beijing's Tiananmen Square, killing hundreds.

The People's Liberation Army garrison for Hong Kong is due to enter the territory in two waves, with 509 marching in at 9.00 p.m. (1300 GMT) on Monday and a further 4,000 sweeping in by land, sea and air just six hours after the midnight handover.
The People's Daily editorial was adamant that the Communist Party was China's -- and Hong Kong's -- saviour.
"The Communist Party of China is the core force to reunify the motherland and vigorously develop the Chinese nation," the editorial said.

It invoked Deng as part of an ongoing campaign to boost the Communist Party's flagging popularity and which has also included a propaganda blitz to boost patriotic sentiment around the Hong Kong handover.

"To further strengthen the party, the most important thing is to hold high Deng Xiaoping's great banner of building socialism with Chinese characteristics," the editorial said, referring to Deng's fig-leaf phrase to justify such un-Marxist concepts as free markets, private enterprise and stock exchanges.
"Deng Xiaoping's theory of building socialism with Chinese characteristics is modern China's Marxism and the strong spiritual pillar of developing the Chinese nation," the editorial said.
